name: Turco-Egyptian Sudan
alt: Egyptian Sudan under Muhammad Ali and the Khedives

successors.name: Mahdist State
successors.text: everything but Wadi Halfa and Suakin: "Kassala and Sennar fell soon after" Khartoum

successors.name: Equatoria Province
successors.text: Equatoria, held by Emin Pasha as an isolated Egyptian outpost until 1889

ledger.x: 20 July 1820: Muhammad Ali's son Ismail Pasha leads the army south from Aswan.
4 November 1820: the Shaygiya fall at Korti.
1821: Kordofan falls after the Battle of Barah, where the Defterdar's army beat a larger Darfuri force.
5 March 1821: Berber submits to Ismail Pasha without a fight.
May 1821: Khartoum becomes the army's headquarters and later Sudan's capital.
14-15 June 1821: Sennar falls and the Funj sultanate ends.
Late 1822: Ismail Pasha is killed at Shendi and the Ja'alin rise.
1823: the Defterdar restores Egyptian control by punitive campaigns.
1840: Kassala and Taka are added to the Egyptian domains.
1855: Fashoda is listed among the later additions.
1865: the Ottoman Empire cedes the Red Sea coast to Egypt.
1870: Samuel Baker establishes Equatoria.
1874: Darfur is conquered and annexed.
August 1881: the Mahdi's followers destroy two Egyptian companies on Aba Island.
1882: El Obeid starves into submission.
1883: Darfur is lost.
1885: Kassala and Sennar fall.
1885: bridge for the rest of the Nile, Gezira and the White Nile.
1885: Equatoria is left as an isolated outpost.
26 January 1885: with Khartoum the Egyptian government in Sudan ends, though the Mahdist War continues against Anglo-Egyptian forces to 1899.
26 January 1885: Khartoum falls.
January 1885: the Turco-Egyptian period ends.

wars.name: Turco-Egyptian conquest of Sudan
wars.outcome: "Turco-Egyptian victory": Dongola, Berber, Sennar and Kordofan taken in 1820-21, the Ja'alin revolt crushed in 1822-23.

wars.name: Mahdist War
wars.outcome: Mahdist victory: Kordofan 1882, Darfur 1883, Khartoum on 26 January 1885, Kassala and Sennar soon after; Wadi Halfa and Suakin stayed Anglo-Egyptian.

certainty.note: The Egyptian frontier on the Nile at Wadi Halfa and the Ethiopian and Equatorial limits are approximate; no source here gives a boundary line.
